programme.title: Britain's Outlaws: Highwaymen, Pirates and Rogues
programme.sub-title: Knights of the Road: The Highwayman's Story
programme.desc: Sam Willis shows that, far from being outsiders, outlaws were very much a product of their time, shaped by national events. He begins with the arrival of a new breed of gentleman criminal out of the ashes of the English Civil War - the highwayman.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Documentary about the tube, the world's oldest underground system. Three million passengers use it every day, and over the past 150 years, it has developed its own history, alongside literature, music and film that have been inspired by it.

programme.title: Inside Museums
programme.desc: Huw Stephens tells the story of the Welsh slate industry with a visit to the National Slate Museum in Llanberis. It's an extraordinary story of ruthless landlords exploiting whole mountains to make vast profits from what is now Snowdonia National Park. Quarrying slate was a brutal business, and working conditions for the poorly paid men were extremely dangerous. In 1900, the longest industrial dispute in British history started with the Great Penrhyn Strike at the quarry in Bethesda.

programme.title: Railway Walks
programme.desc: Julia's first walking foray into Scotland has a very distinct flavour to it: whisky! The Speyside Way is one of Scotland's great walking routes, and between the villages of Craigellachie and Ballindaloch it follows the route of the railway that once served a remote area and a world-famous drinks industry.

programme.title: Turner: The Man Who Painted Britain
programme.desc: While Joseph Mallord William Turner is considered by many to be Britain's greatest landscape painter, his private life reveals a man of extremes and contradictions. This is a look at the extraordinary story of a brilliant self-made man.

programme.title: Inside Museums
programme.desc: Marie-Louise Muir discovers the beauty of everyday objects, found at homes in Northern Ireland at the turn of the 20th century. These include Harnen Stands used to toast oatcakes in front of an open fire and one of the finest examples of crazy patchwork quilts seen in any British museum.

programme.title: Railway Walks
programme.desc: The backstreets of Weymouth seem an unlikely spot to explore railway history, but Julia discovers there was once a short railway that ran south from Weymouth and across the unique coastal features of Chesil Beach and Portland. The walk is the ideal platform for learning about the history of Portland Harbour and the tied isle's most famous export, Portland stone.

programme.title: The Magic of Mushrooms
programme.desc: Professor Richard Fortey delves into the fascinating and normally hidden kingdom of fungi. From their spectacular birth, to their final explosive death, Richard reveals a remarkable world that few of us even realise exists.

programme.title: The Brontes at the BBC
programme.desc: An exploration of the BBC's long love affair with the lives and works of the Bronte sisters, Charlotte, Emily and Anne. For over half a century, the ill-fated literary dynasty has proved irresistible to drama and documentary makers alike, keen to re-invent their novels for new audiences.

programme.title: Ruth Wilson and Toby Stephens Remember... Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Actors Ruth Wilson and Toby Stephens look back on the 2006 TV adaptation of Charlotte Bronte's `Jane Eyre'. The reunited pair look back on the production and share their memories of being part of the cast.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Dramatisation of Charlotte Brontë's classic novel. After surviving the cruel regime of a harsh charity school, orphan Jane Eyre takes a job as a governess at Thornfield Hall. Here, she finds herself increasingly attracted to her enigmatic master, Mr Rochester, but Jane's peaceful existence is shattered when strange events in the night threaten danger.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Jane finds she has a rival for Rochester's attentions in the beautiful Blanche Ingram, and the gossip is that Rochester will soon propose marriage. Meanwhile, a mysterious visitor from overseas brings great trouble to Thornfield, and Jane is called to Rochester's aid once again.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Jane finds she has a rival for Rochester's attentions in the beautiful Blanche Ingram, and the gossip is that Rochester will soon propose marriage. Meanwhile, a mysterious visitor from overseas brings great trouble to Thornfield, and Jane is called to Rochester's aid once again.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: On her deathbed, Aunt Reed reveals important information about Jane's family which she has hidden for years. Returning to Thornfield, Jane expects Rochester to wed Blanche Ingram and is shocked by an altogether different marriage proposal. Just as Jane's dreams are about to come true, she discovers a terrible secret from the past that could destroy everything.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Having left Thornfield, a heartbroken Jane finds herself alone, penniless and starving on the moors. She lies down in a final act of surrender to the elements, but is rescued by clergyman St John Rivers who, together with his sisters, nurses her back to health. Jane begins a new life as a teacher, but when Rivers proposes marriage she thinks she hears Rochester call out her name and knows she must go back to Thornfield.

programme.title: The Bronte Business
programme.desc: First transmitted in 1977, Joan Bakewell visits Haworth in Yorkshire, home of the Brontes, to see the setting in which the novelists worked.
